title: Finite-strain logarithmic J2 material and global paths
purpose: Verify the local multiplicative update, generic quadrature transaction, gated total-Lagrangian consumer, distributed assembly, and cross-partition restart before the public finite-element workflow is promoted.
physics: three-dimensional rate-independent finite-strain J2 plasticity with quadratic Hencky elasticity and linear isotropic hardening

execution.command: python -m pytest -q tests/test_finite_strain_plasticity.py; mpirun -n 2 python tests/finite_strain_j2_mpi_driver.py; run tests/portable_finite_strain_j2_driver.py in 2-to-1 and 1-to-2 rank workflows
execution.evidence: Independent material paths exercise rigid and superposed rotations, isochoric plastic flow, yield consistency, unloading and reversal, fixed-old-state tangent comparison, atomic quadrature commit or rollback, serial and two-rank 3D displacement-controlled global patches, forced physical cutback, and portable restart after changing MPI rank count.

observables: Cauchy stress under rigid and superposed rotations.
Equivalent plastic strain and determinant of the plastic deformation gradient.
Updated Kirchhoff equivalent stress relative to the isotropically hardened yield radius.
Relative error between the returned dP/dF and an independent centered derivative.
Committed and trial state vectors before and after success or intentional local failure.
Accepted and rejected global load increments, Newton residuals, and maximum PEEQ increment.
Serial/distributed terminal displacement and owned-point PEEQ extrema.
Restored nodal fields, quadrature state, load coordinate, and increment ledger across changed MPI partitions.
acceptance: Rigid rotation is stress free and superposed rotation covariantly rotates stress without changing scalar history.
A plastic path keeps det(Fp) equal to one and returns to the current yield surface.
An elastic unloading leaves state unchanged while a sufficiently large reverse path cannot reduce accumulated plastic strain.
Elastic and plastic discrete tangents satisfy the declared numerical relative-error tolerance.
A failed local batch restores all trial fields and a successful accepted batch commits every state variable atomically.
The total-Lagrangian patch reaches its prescribed displacement, consumes the neutral tangent, and cuts back an otherwise converged increment whose PEEQ change exceeds the declared limit.
Two-rank assembly preserves the prescribed deformation and uniform material state.
Two-to-one and one-to-two rank restart workflows recover and complete the same accepted loading path.
limitations: The global evidence consists of controlled patch paths; it is not an independent external structural validation.
The returned tangent is a correctness-first numerical derivative rather than the final analytical production tangent.
An external finite-strain plasticity structure comparison and production-performance tangent remain promotion gates.
